3. Controlled pinning without constructing a Gibbs logarithm

The positive network supports more than direct sampling. It has a constructive normalization operation that remains controlled after arbitrarily unlikely product outcomes are pinned.

This addresses the extra operation emphasized in Putterman–Zlokapa–Cotler: their Gibbs sampler pays normalization after pinning, rather than obtaining it from additive expectations alone. Their finite-arity Pauli Hamiltonian and local-strength assumptions remain substantive. arxiv.org <https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28536v2?utm_source=chatgpt.com>


Uniform posterior control

Suppose an actual network vertex satisfies
$\Phi=(1-q)\mathcal E+q\Psi,
\qquad
\Psi\le_{\mathrm{cp}}c\mathcal E.$
Fix all other branch choices and any final positive event $Y$. Let $a_0,a_1$ be its probabilities with $\mathcal E,\Psi$ at this vertex. CP order gives $a_1\le ca_0$, hence
$\boxed{
\Pr(\text{residual branch}\mid Y,\text{other branches})
\le
\frac{cq}{1-q+cq}.
}
\tag{14}$
If $a_0=0$, then $a_1=0$; there is no positive-probability exception.

The bound survives averaging over unspecified branches. It applies even when $Y$ is exponentially unlikely. No additive error has been divided by a tiny prefix probability.


Exact positive scalar representation

For each nonzero pinned POVM effect define
$A_i=\frac{M_i}{\tau_i(M_i)},
\qquad \tau_i(M_i)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}M_i}{2}.$
Then
$A_i\ge0,\qquad \tau_i(A_i)=1,\qquad \|A_i\|_\infty\le2.
\tag{15}$
The norm bound is independent of how small the original outcome probability is.

Let $P_0(y)$ be the output-pin probability when every gate takes its reset branch. For an active branch set $F$, the reset cuts give
$\frac{P(y\mid F)}{P_0(y)}
=
\prod_{C\in\operatorname{components}(F)}r_C(y).
\tag{16}$
Replacing the gates of one component in CP order yields
$2^{-|C|}\le r_C(y)\le(3/2)^{|C|}.
\tag{17}$
It follows exactly that
$P(y)=P_0(y)(1-q)^V Z_y,$
where
$Z_y=
\sum_{\text{compatible collections }\Gamma}
\prod_{C\in\Gamma}w_C(y),
\qquad
w_C(y)=
\left(\frac q{1-q}\right)^{|C|}r_C(y).
\tag{18}$
The components are incompatible when they overlap or are adjacent in the gate graph.

This is a positive scalar polymer model of channel-history components. It makes no assertion about the spatial logarithm of the quantum output state.

The chosen $q$ satisfies a Kotecký–Preiss bound with an additional exponent
